articles.title: How China is preparing for the risk of AI escaping human control
articles.summary: China is tightening regulations, safety standards, and state oversight to address the growing risk that increasingly autonomous AI systems could evade safeguards, replicate themselves, or act beyond human control. The government aims to establish stricter rules and monitoring mechanisms to ensure AI development remains within safe boundaries.

articles.title: Three appointed high court judges
articles.summary: The Judicial Council has appointed three individuals as high court judges: Supreme Court Registrar Bhadrakali Pokharel, District Judge Himlal Belbase, and Gajendra Bahadur Singh. Alongside these appointments, the council also approved several judicial transfers and new postings within the Nepalese judiciary.

articles.title: David Warner joins Kathmandu Gorkhas for NPL Season 3
articles.summary: Australian cricket star David Warner, a multiple World Cup winner, has been signed as the third overseas player for Kathmandu Gorkhas ahead of the third season of Nepal's National Premier League (NPL). The announcement was made on Tuesday, highlighting the team's effort to boost its squad with international talent for the upcoming competition.

articles.title: Four die in three weeks as scrub typhus spreads in Salyan
articles.summary: An outbreak of scrub typhus in Salyan district has claimed four lives within three weeks. Over 100 residents of Darma Rural Municipality have tested positive, and local health facilities are reporting three to four new cases daily. Health officials warn that the disease is spreading rapidly and urge the community to seek prompt medical attention and adopt preventive measures. The situation highlights ongoing challenges in disease surveillance and healthcare access in rural Nepal.

articles.title: Four killed in microbus crash in Makwanpur
articles.summary: A microbus traveling toward Hetauda crashed in Makwanpur, Nepal, resulting in four fatalities. The accident was reported by the Kathmandu Post.

articles.title: Nepal’s border map is a shared national commitment, says Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal
articles.summary: Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the country's border map, covering Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura, is a shared national commitment and cannot be treated as 'old baggage'.

articles.title: DoFE seeks answers from 250 agencies selected by Malaysia to recruit workers
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Employment (DoFE) has given 250 agencies selected by Malaysia to recruit workers a seven‑day deadline to explain the criteria and process used for their selection.

articles.title: Kremlin welcomes Trump’s idea of energy truce with Ukraine, calls for sanctions removal
articles.summary: The Kremlin has expressed support for former US President Donald Trump's proposal of an energy truce with Ukraine, urging the removal of sanctions against Russia. While Ukraine endures frequent Russian strikes on its energy facilities and argues that its refineries are legitimate military targets, Moscow sees the truce as a step toward easing the energy war and improving diplomatic ties.

articles.title: Pelega hill in Nawalparasi has been smoking for years. Now experts want answers
articles.summary: Residents of Nawalparasi district have long observed smoke rising from various spots on Pelega Hill, but the phenomenon has intensified in recent months, prompting concern among locals. The persistent emissions have raised questions about possible underground fires, gas leaks, or other environmental hazards. Experts from the Nepalese Ministry of Forests and Environment, as well as local universities, have been called to investigate the source and assess health risks for nearby communities. Authorities are under pressure to provide answers and mitigate any potential danger to the region’s population and ecosystem.

articles.title: More tigers, more conflict, but too little room for those rescued
articles.summary: Nepal’s tiger population has risen to 429, intensifying human‑tiger conflicts. However, the country’s sole zoo and rescue centres are ill‑equipped, lacking sufficient space and proper facilities to accommodate tigers rescued from settlements or those too old or injured to survive in the wild.

articles.title: Repeated Tatopani closures deepen uncertainty for traders
articles.summary: Repeated shutdowns of the Tatopani border crossing between Nepal and China have left over 45 containers stranded in China, deepening uncertainty for Nepali traders. Years of intermittent closures have resulted in substantial financial losses for businesses that rely on this trade route, disrupting supply chains and raising concerns about the reliability of cross‑border commerce. Traders fear further economic damage if the situation persists, urging authorities to find a lasting solution.

articles.title: Kantipur Max secures exclusive Nepal rights for 20th Asian Games
articles.summary: Kantipur Max has obtained exclusive rights to broadcast the 20th Asian Games (Aichi-Nagoya) in Nepal. The channel will provide live coverage of the event, where Nepal's 184‑member delegation will compete across 21 sports. The deal enhances sports broadcasting in the country and highlights Nepal's participation in the regional multi‑sport competition.

articles.title: Local governments call for climate justice and compensation at Mustang conference
articles.summary: Representatives from 431 local governments and 41 district coordination committees gathered in Jomsom, Mustang, to demand climate justice and compensation, emphasizing the escalating impacts of climate change on Nepal's mountain communities.

articles.title: How not to worry about the AI revolution and the law of unintended consequences?
articles.summary: The article discusses public anxiety surrounding the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, warning against the law of unintended consequences that can arise from unchecked AI deployment. It argues that instead of fearing AI, societies should harness its predictive capabilities to monitor natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods, and landslides, thereby improving early warning systems and disaster response. The piece calls for responsible policy frameworks, interdisciplinary collaboration, and investment in AI-driven environmental monitoring to turn a perceived threat into a tool for safeguarding Nepal’s vulnerable communities.

articles.title: How disasters create fertile ground for human trafficking
articles.summary: The article examines how natural and man‑made disasters in Nepal create conditions that traffickers exploit. It outlines how displacement, loss of livelihoods, weakened law enforcement, and disrupted community networks leave victims—especially women and children—vulnerable to being lured or forced into labor and sexual exploitation. The piece highlights recent earthquakes and floods as case studies, noting spikes in trafficking reports following each event. It also discusses the role of NGOs, government agencies, and international bodies in identifying and rescuing victims, while stressing the need for stronger disaster‑response frameworks that integrate anti‑trafficking measures. The author calls for coordinated policy reforms, better data collection, and community awareness to prevent traffickers from turning disaster‑stricken areas into fertile ground for their crimes.

articles.title: A single landslide has choked Kathmandu for weeks. Dependable backup routes must be built
articles.summary: A landslide on the Prithvi Highway has blocked traffic into Kathmandu for weeks, causing major disruption to commuters and freight. The incident highlights the city's over‑reliance on a single main artery and the urgent need for reliable alternative routes and better disaster‑response planning. Authorities are urged to develop and maintain backup roads to ensure connectivity during future natural events.

articles.title: Their loved ones are gone. The law says they are still missing
articles.summary: Families of victims swept away by the August 26 flood in Kathmandu are conducting funeral rites without bodies, yet they cannot obtain death certificates, preventing them from accessing relief, compensation, insurance and other entitlements.

articles.title: Judicial Council starts high court appointments, leaves Supreme Court vacancies unresolved
articles.summary: The Judicial Council has started appointing judges to high courts, but has not addressed the vacancies in the Supreme Court, drawing criticism from judges and the Nepal Bar Association.

articles.title: NPL gets bigger with David Warner’s announcement by Kathmandu Gorkhas
articles.summary: The Nepal Premier League (NPL) is set to expand its profile as former Australian opening batsman David Warner, a winner of major tournaments across Test, ODI and T20 formats, has announced his participation in the league's upcoming third season. Warner will join the Kathmandu Gorkhas franchise, bringing international star power and heightened interest to Nepalese cricket.

articles.title: Real estate market shows signs of recovery after prolonged slowdown
articles.summary: The Nepalese real estate market is showing signs of recovery after a prolonged slowdown, with transaction volume and value rising in the last fiscal year. The rebound is driven by higher bank lending and renewed buyer confidence.

articles.title: Nepal needs joint effort to fight joint pain
articles.summary: Improving understanding, ethical care, and early management can enhance outcomes for Nepalis suffering from osteoarthritis, highlighting the need for a coordinated national effort to address joint pain.

articles.title: Rohit Paudel fined for breaching ICC code in UAE final
articles.summary: Rohit Paudel, along with UAE players Adeeb Usmani and Khuzaima Tanveer, were fined for breaching the ICC's code of conduct during the UAE final. The disciplinary action highlights the governing body's enforcement of conduct standards in international cricket matches.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia issues wide-ranging security alerts after week of strikes
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has issued broad security alerts for the holy cities of Mecca and Jeddah after a week of Houthi missile and drone strikes and the group's advances along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. The alerts highlight heightened risks to Saudi oil export facilities and international shipping lanes in the Red Sea, prompting heightened military and civilian preparedness. The developments underscore escalating regional tensions and the potential for wider disruption of global energy supplies.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran says dropping Macklemore from US concert tour was not his decision
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran clarified that the removal of rapper Macklemore from his U.S. concert tour was not his decision. According to Sheeran, the tour promoter dropped Macklemore after several venues warned they would refuse to host shows featuring the rapper. The move sparked backlash, leading several opening acts and members of Sheeran's touring band to quit in solidarity with Macklemore.

articles.title: India renews Nepal’s power import permit but leaves export approvals pending
articles.summary: India has renewed Nepal's permit to import electricity, ensuring continued supply of Indian power during Nepal's winter months. However, the renewal did not include approvals for three Nepali hydropower projects that seek to export surplus electricity generated during the monsoon season. The pending export permits hinder Nepal's plans to monetize excess power, creating uncertainty for the projects' investors and for Nepal's broader strategy to become a regional electricity exporter. The decision reflects ongoing diplomatic and commercial negotiations between the two neighbors over cross‑border energy trade.
